name: IL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+34 district lean makes Democrats overwhelming favorites to hold the seat
Open seat after Danny Davis's retirement removes incumbent advantage but not the partisan floor
La Shawn Ford's roughly 13-to-1 fundraising edge over Chad Koppie, who has almost no cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 97%
model.rationale: The district's D+34 partisan lean and Ford's dominant fundraising advantage over a barely funded Republican opponent make the seat effectively out of reach for the GOP, even with no incumbent on the ballot. With no public polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Ford or unusually low Democratic turnout in a low-profile open-seat race could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois's 7th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, and Danny Davis's retirement leaves it open but still firmly in the party's column. La Shawn Ford enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised roughly $819,000 to Republican Chad Koppie's $60,000, and Koppie ends the cycle with almost no cash on hand. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97%.

The main sources of uncertainty are the absence of recent public polling and the open-seat dynamic, which removes the incumbent's personal vote. Outside groups have spent heavily opposing Ford, largely a reflection of a contested primary, but nothing suggests that endangers the seat in November. Fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic win in the high-twenty-point range.
